messages:
eli: quick heads-up — saw a regression on canary 2026-03-16 02:10 UTC. p99 up ~20% on small-seq workloads. digging into traces now.
priya: ugh, thanks for flagging. any obvious root cause from flamegraphs?
eli: early signal points to kernel selection latch. runtime kept picking FlashAttention for many tiny requests which increased kernel setup cost and prevented decent token coalescing. queues were shallow but high-churn.
sam: can you paste the profiler snippet?
eli: sure — pasted from the run: 
```
# perf summary
flash_attn_setup  35.2 ms (avg)
matmul_qk        4.8 ms
kv_page_faults   78 / sec (paged-kv working set thrash)
batch_size_tokens avg=22 median=4
p99_latency      +120 ms
```
Link: https://perf.redwood/profiler/trace/abc123 (flamegraph.svg)
priya: interesting — so two issues: high kernel setup for FlashAttention and paged-KV noise creating page faults on lots of tiny KV hits. both reduce effective batching.
jonathan: small requests tend to force short-lived allocations; paged KV does extra work per miss. if kernel choice is latched per-connection or per-model-version it can be sticky and stop the coalescer from grouping tokens.
eli: exactly. our current latch rule: pick highest-throughput kernel when predicted avg_seq >= 64 OR batch_tokens_est >= 1024, then latch for 30s. that interacts badly with spiky arrival rate.
sam: what if we make kernel latch depend on observed batch_tokens rather than predicted avg_seq? or add a lower bound on min_batch_tokens before latching to FlashAttention?
priya: I sketched a few experiments in the notebook: (1) token_budget_threshold for Flash = 256 instead of 1024, (2) dynamic hysteresis: require 3 consecutive batches above threshold to latch, (3) allow per-batch kernel decision when batch_size_tokens < 128.
eli: I ran a quick canary with (2) and (3) — results promising: batch coalescing improved, p99 dropped ~10% vs bad run. but paged-KV still noisy.
jonathan: for paged-KV we could add short-lived prefetch for active sessions or increase in-memory working set for hot keys — but that has memory cost. maybe prefer smaller kernels that are KV-friendly when pagefaults spike.
sam: concrete plan: runtime/pr/456 change-latch-policy branch does: - switch latch trigger to observed batch_tokens; - add hysteresis count=3; - fallback kernel preference when kv_page_fault_rate > 50/s. I'll open PR.
eli: please include perf-run config and canary plan (route 10% traffic to dedicated pool). add a metric: kernel_latch_state{kernel="flash",count} and kv_page_fault_rate per GPU.
priya: also add a micro-benchmark that simulates heavy tiny-seq arrival (poisson with mean 30 tokens) so we can validate locally.
jonathan: small suggestion: implement a soft-latch weight instead of boolean latch — keep a score per kernel that decays and choose largest score each decision. that smooths weird spikes.
sam: nice, I'll prototype soft-latch + hysteresis. will run perf-bot nightly job and post results.
perf-bot: nightly regression alert (2026-03-17): canary-2026-03-16 showed p99 delta +18% -> investigating: https://perf.redwood/alerts/7890
eli: thanks. next steps: sam to push PR and schedule 10% canary tomorrow, priya to add micro-bench harness, jonathan to sketch KV prefetch tradeoffs. I'll collate notes into the runbook.
priya: ack. I'll also add a dashboard card that shows batch_tokens distribution (bucketed) + kernel selection heatmap per model.
sam: PR created: https://git.redwood/infra/runtime/pull/456 — includes config flags: `min_batch_tokens_for_flash=256`, `latch_hysteresis=3`, `kv_fault_fallback=true`. running unit + perf.
eli: awesome. if canary looks good we'll roll to 50% and revisit memory vs latency for KV prefetch. thanks team :thumbsup:
